demonstrated: cross_instance_shared_budget: app-a admitted on Gateway A (HTTP 200), then denied on Gateway B (HTTP 429, X-RateLimit-Remaining-Tokens: 0) for the same shared Valkey ledger
per_app_isolation: app-b admitted on Gateway B (HTTP 200) immediately after app-a's exhaustion in the same Valkey namespace
per_app_isolation: app-c admitted on Gateway A (HTTP 200) on its own independent, untouched budget
reservation_admission: each admitted request reserved its estimate_tokens cost atomically via the shared ledger before the response was known

window_recovery: app-a, previously denied, is admitted again on Gateway A (HTTP 200) once the 10s sliding window aged its earlier reservation out -- no manual reset, no restart, budget recovers purely because the window advanced
configured: window: 10s sliding window (shortened from the README's default 1h purely so the recording could show a full deny -> recover cycle in a watchable clip; the mechanism is identical at any window size)
backend: valkey, shared namespace across both gateway replicas

validation.live_gates: 5 requireGate assertions passed during recording against a live docker-compose stack (see playwright/record.mjs): app-a admitted on A, app-a denied on B (remaining=0), app-b admitted on B, app-c admitted on A, app-a re-admitted on A after the window aged out

limitations: No OPENAI_API_KEY was available in this environment: narration audio used a local macOS `say` TTS fallback instead of the toolkit's OpenAI TTS (scripts/generate-narration.sh), and narration.srt caption timing is an approximate proportional-duration estimate rather than a real Whisper transcription (scripts/generate-captions.sh). Both are flagged deviations, not canonical toolkit output -- re-run with OPENAI_API_KEY set to get the toolkit's default pipeline.

No exact_trace evidence gate: this scenario is a single-hop admission decision with no cross-service routing, so there is no distributed trace to correlate. Evidence is instead the exact HTTP status/headers returned by the live gateways, asserted via requireGate during recording.

The browser dashboard (../dashboard/) is a demo-only recording convenience wrapping the same HTTP contract as the docker-compose README's curl walkthrough; it is not part of the Praxis AI filter chain and ships only with this recording, not upstream.
App names (app-a/app-b/app-c) are placeholders. The real customer scenario's application names are intentionally excluded (NDA) and enforced via production.yaml's redaction.deny list.

This remains early exploratory work validating ai#658's sliding-window design and the ai#129 bucket-key proposal, not a substitute for their own review threads -- see the parent README's "Current scope" section.

The window is a fixed 10s sliding window in this build. Neither ai#658 nor ai#121 specifies an algorithm (sliding window vs. token bucket vs. fixed window); praxis#551 (a separate, core-proxy rate-limit issue) already proposes per-rule algorithm choice and configurable window duration -- see the parent README's "Open design questions" section for the follow-up raised there.
